Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our procurement redline of the DPA (FinServeCo_DPA_redlines_20261101.pdf). - Whether you will accept SCCs by reference + an Annex with the SCCs text, or if you need an embedded copy;

Hi Emma — thanks for the redline.

Quick answers:
- We are generally fine to accept SCCs by reference with an Annex that includes the SCC text; that keeps the main DPA tidier and still legally robust.
- We prefer a combined envelope (DPA + UK IDTA) so you don't have to sign two separate docs, but we can separate if your legal insists.
- We'll aim to return a clean counter by COB Nov 5.

Next steps from our side: I'll loop in Karthik (legal/inference compliance) and Monica (security/compliance evidence) to draft a counter and assemble the subprocessor pack. Please share the name and email of your intended signer (CPO/GC) so we can set signing order. Also will you accept DocuSign? If so, please confirm whether DocuSign is acceptable for both Redwood and FinServeCo for the UK addendum.

I'll attach an internal tracker and eSign flow diagram as we firm things up.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Monica — quick technical/legal notes after a first pass on FinServeCo's redline: 

1) SCCs/version: Their redline doesn't specify which SCC iteration; we should propose the EU SCCs (2021) and include them as Annex II. That avoids ambiguity on which controller/processor clauses apply.
2) UK IDTA: we can accept the UK Addendum with two small edits to the transfer impact paragraph — change to "reasonable efforts" + carveouts for law enforcement requests.
3) Subprocessors: provide the current subprocessor list and ISO/SOC evidence; we should offer to provide a timeline for onboarding any new subprocessors they call out.
4) Section 7.3 (liability/transfer language): they tightened transfer liability; recommend countering to preserve Redwood's standard limiter with carveouts for willful misconduct.

Proposed ops: legal to issue counter-redline (tracked in SCCs_tracker.xlsx), security to prepare proof bundle (SOC 2 cert + data flow diagram). We'll offer DocuSign combined envelope but note FinServeCo may prefer separate execution of the UK addendum — give them both options.

I'll draft the counter for Marissa to review today.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: SCCs-compatibility-notes.txt, subprocessor-evidence-list (internal)

Thanks Karthik and Marissa — few clarifications from our side: 
- Our legal team wants either the SCCs embedded or an Annex with the full text (Annex preferred if the references are explicit).
- Procurement prefers the UK IDTA to be executed in the same eSign flow if possible (avoids separate routing). If Redwood proposes a combined envelope, we'll confirm internally but we prefer a single envelope.
- We'll need the subprocessor list and SOC 2 report uploaded to our procurement portal (https://procure.finservco.com/upload/HS-78923). Can Redwood confirm when you'll publish those items?

We would like a counter by EOD Nov 5 to keep the internal approval calendar on track.

Emma
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: draft counter & eSign choreography

Team — outline for the counter we will send to Emma today: 
1) Accept SCCs by reference + include SCC 2021 text as Annex A; call out controller/processor roles clearly.
2) UK IDTA: accept as addendum; propose to include it within the same DocuSign envelope but allow FinServeCo to separate if their legal insists. Add one minor change to transfer impact language: "Redwood will take commercially reasonable measures to mitigate transfer risks; Redwood retains the right to notify and seek written acceptance for residual risks."
3) Liability: push back on expanding transfer liability; preserve standard cap but carve out for gross negligence/willful misconduct and data breach regulatory fines tied to Redwood's failure to implement controls.
4) Subprocessor evidence: publish current subprocessor list and SOC 2 link today and commit to responding to any evidence questions within 3 business days.
5) eSign flow: propose a single DocuSign envelope with two signers on FinServeCo side (CPO then GC) and one signer at Redwood (COO). Include eSign-flow-diagram.png in our reply so procurement can see routing.

Please review and let me know if I should temper any of the language before I send the counter. If we get their acceptance on combined envelope, we'll prepare the DocuSign draft and share a link.

Marissa
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
